summary:
Our project, **MISSION: BEYOND EARTH**, is an interactive space mission simulation designed to help children experience the challenges of being an astronaut, learn about space exploration, and develop their scientific thinking skills.

To achieve this goal, we designed mission scenarios based on exploring the Moon and Mars, astronaut training, and a base management system. Users experience realistic space challenges by analyzing situations, managing resources, and making their own decisions.

Through astronaut training and the base management system, players learn to manage essential resources such as energy, oxygen, radiation protection, and food supplies. Every decision matters: different choices lead to different outcomes and multiple possible endings.

**A key feature of our project is the integration of up-to-date NASA DONKI (Space Weather Database) data.** The simulation retrieves and displays the latest available space weather events, including solar flares, connecting real-time space weather information with in-game mission scenarios. This allows players to observe current solar activity, understand potential space weather risks, and explore how such events can influence astronaut safety, resource management, and mission decisions.

Our project also draws on scientific data and research from NASA and CSA, including LRO, OSDR, and MOXIE.

**Don’t just learn about space. Experience the decisions that shape the future of space exploration.**
details:
MISSION: BEYOND EARTH

Project Details and Use of AI

Our project, MISSION: BEYOND EARTH, is an interactive, browser-based space mission simulation designed to help children and young people experience the challenges astronauts may face instead of learning about space exploration only through theory. Our main goal is to increase interest in space science while developing scientific thinking, problem-solving, and decision-making skills.

We combined Moon and Mars exploration, astronaut training, and space base management into one simulation. Players choose their mission destination and training level before beginning their journey. Throughout the missions, they must make decisions while considering essential factors such as energy, oxygen, food supplies, radiation, equipment safety, and mission conditions. Astronaut safety, efficient resource management, and changing space conditions are among the main factors guiding our design.

One of our project’s key features is the integration of NASA’s DONKI (Space Weather Database) API. Using JavaScript’s fetch() method, the simulation retrieves the latest available space weather events and brings real scientific information into the game. This allows players to connect actual space weather conditions with mission scenarios. We also incorporated scientific research and data associated with NASA sources, including LRO, OSDR, and MOXIE.

Our multiple-ending system makes every decision meaningful. Different choices lead to different consequences and mission outcomes, allowing players to experience how their decisions affect the success of a space mission.

What makes our project creative and distinctive is the combination of real NASA scientific data with an interactive, decision-based gameplay experience. Instead of presenting space information through static lessons, we allow players to experience astronaut challenges, manage a space base, respond to changing mission conditions, and face the consequences of their own decisions. The integration of NASA DONKI data, multiple mission scenarios, and different possible endings creates an educational experience in which science and gameplay work together. This approach transforms space exploration from passive learning into active discovery.

Visual Studio Code was used as our main software development environment. We developed our simulation using three core web technologies: HTML5, CSS3, and JavaScript. HTML5 was used to build the structure of the game, including its screens, panels, and interactive elements. CSS3 was used to create the visual design, space-themed atmosphere, neon effects, progress bars, and screen transitions. JavaScript powered the game’s interactive mechanics, including resource management, mission decisions, changing scenarios, and retrieving space weather data from NASA’s official DONKI API using the fetch() method. The simulation runs in a standard web browser without requiring additional specialized hardware.

Artificial intelligence tools, including Gemini and ChatGPT, were used during different stages of our project’s development. Gemini was used to assist with coding, debugging, and solving technical problems, while ChatGPT supported the project’s design process, interface planning, brainstorming, and creative development. These tools served as assistants throughout the development process, while the project concept, mission scenarios, gameplay decisions, design choices, testing, and final implementation were shaped through our team’s collaborative work.

Our project was developed through teamwork, with each member contributing to the creative and development process. Our voice-over was recorded by our team.

Our vision is to transform space from something people simply learn about into a world they can explore, experience, and make decisions in.

Don’t just learn about space. Experience the decisions that shape the future of space exploration.
